outcome: histopathological study of the fallopian tube
cohort: The study included 103 women aged 32-35 years undergoing permanent sterilisation during caesarean section in India.
finding: Bilateral salpingectomy does not significantly affect ovarian reserve in the short term (six months) compared to bilateral tubectomy, though it requires approximately 10 minutes more surgery time.
mod_finding: The study found that when performed during caesarean section, bilateral salpingectomy is comparable to traditional bilateral tubectomy regarding ovarian reserve and complications, suggesting its potential adoption as a routine sterilisation method during this mode of birth.
